questions.question: In a certain code language, 'BED' is written as '122' and 'CAB' is written as '37'. How will 'ADD' be written in that code language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6e81f3ed21fddc72dd7e74439132a9341e1cd67dad9da66ee032ef789862eab.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Logic: **(Sum of the place value of all numbers)² + 1 = Code of the word**.

'BED' is written as '122'

⇒ (2 + 5 + 4)² +1

⇒ 11² + 1 = 122.

'CAB' is written as '37'

⇒ (3 + 1 + 2)2 +1

⇒ 62 + 1 = 37.

Similarly, for **'ADD'**

**⇒ (1 + 4 + 4)2 +1**

**⇒ 92 + 1 = 82.**

So, 'ADD' will be written as '82'.

Hence, the correct answer is **"82"**.

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers shares the same relationship in set as that shared by the numbers in the given set.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits.

E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

(12, 144, 1728)

(6, 36, 216)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **(1st number)² = 2nd number,**

**(1st number)3**** = 3rd number**.

Now,

for, (12, 144, 1728)

⇒ (12)² = 144,

⇒ (12)3 = 1728.

for, (6, 36, 216)

⇒ (6)2 = 36,

⇒ (6)3 = 216.

Similarly, for **(10, 100, 1000)**

**⇒ (10)2 = 100,**

**⇒ (10)3 = 1000.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

questions.question:
How many triangles are there in the given figure?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/432b717705afd22d3d890aa7d5934339d56b176568a878709f1b1ba522dbea79.png]
questions.solution:
The triangles are:
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/432b717705afd22d3d890aa7d5934339d56b176568a878709f1b1ba522dbea79.png] 

The triangles in the figure can be counted by breaking the figure down into its components.

1. The number of single, smallest triangles is 8.

2. The number of triangles formed by combining 2 components is 4.

3. The number of triangles formed by combining 3 components is 4.

4. The number of triangles formed by combining 4 or more components is 4.

Total triangles = 8 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 20.

So, there are 20 triangles in the given figure.

Hence, the correct answer is "20".

questions.question: If 739 R 635 = 52 and 814 R 122 = 346, then 532 R 220 =?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Consider **R as '-' then divide by 2**.

Given,

For, 739 R 635 = 52,

⇒ (739 - 635) ÷ 2

⇒ 104 ÷ 2 = 52. 

For, 814 R 122 = 346,

⇒ (814 - 122) ÷ 2

⇒ 692 ÷ 2 = 346.

Similarly, for **532 R 220 = ?**

**⇒ (532 - 220) ÷ 2**

**⇒ 312 ÷ 2 = 156.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"156"**.

questions.question:
After interchanging the given two signs what will be the values of expression (I) and (II) respectively?

+ and −

I. 45 + 15 × 30 ÷ 10 − 25

II. 6 × 9 + 5 − 8 ÷ 4
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation I. 45 + 15 × 30 ÷ 10 − 25

Now, if '+ and -' are interchanged, then:

⇒ 45 - 15 × __**30 ÷ 10**__ + 25

⇒ 45 - __**15 × 3**__ + 25

⇒ __**45**__ - 45 __**+ 25**__

⇒ __**7**0 - 45__ = 25.

Given equation II: 6 × 9 + 5 − 8 ÷ 4

Now, if '+ and -' are interchanged, then:

⇒ 6 × 9 - 5 + __**8 ÷ 4**__

⇒ __**6 × 9**__ - 5 + 2

⇒ __**54**__ - 5 __**+ 2**__

⇒ __56 - 5__ = 51.

Here, the correct values are '25 and 51'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers shares the same relationship in set as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

(8, 5, 39)

(14, 11, 75)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **(1st number + 2nd number) × 3 = 3rd number**.

Now,

For, (8, 5, 39)

⇒ (8 + 5) × 3

⇒ 13 × 3 = 39.

For, (14, 11, 75)

⇒ (14 + 11) × 3

⇒ 25 × 3 = 75.

Similarly, for **(7, 4, 33)**

**⇒ (7 + 4) × 3**

**⇒ 11 × 3 = 33.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number)² -(2nd number)² = 3rd number.

Now,

For, (8, 5, 39)

⇒ 8² - 5² 

⇒ 64 - 25 = 39.

For, (14, 11, 75)

⇒ (14)² - (11)² 

⇒ 196 - 121 = 75.

Similarly, for (7, 4, 33)

⇒ 7² - 4²

⇒ 49 - 16 = 33.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question:
In the question two statements are given, followed by two conclusions, I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions, if any, follows from the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. No mobile is an electronic item.

II. All electronic items are costly.

**Conclusions:**

I. No costly is a mobile.

II. Some costly are mobile.

options.text: Both conclusion I and II follow.
Either conclusion I or II follow.

questions.solution:
Statements:

I. No mobile is an electronic item.

II. All electronic items are costly.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9217507173c7234d429402b465e0c31bcbe2148d8daa7fb91625ff4bce9e8c73.png] 

Conclusion:

I. No costly is a mobile - False (No definite relation given between costly and mobile, so it can be possible only).

II. Some costly are mobile - False (No definite relation given between costly and mobile, so it can be possible only).

Here, Conclusion I and III forms complementary pair for either-or.

So, Either conclusion I or II follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

Conditions of Either-or case:

1. The elements should be the same in both the statements.

2. Both the conclusions should be false individually.

3. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair)

- The two complementary pairs are:

1) All + Some not

2) No + Some

Note: Some + Some not is not considered under Either -or case.
